g_policy.reason: The user chooses to play the card's game, and the offer copy states the reward (priority routing, 60 minutes). Declining leaves the menu unchanged, and a failed load or verification has its own path.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of priority routing, which is an in-app queue benefit and not cash or anything cash-like.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger event says the card 'only goes to users whose chats are mostly long roleplay stories'. That targeting depends on the content and topic of users' chats, not on an app event.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The idea adds a temporary boost and removes or caps nothing free users have today. Replies keep their normal speed if the user declines.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card sits in the profile menu drawer (s09), a sheet over the non-chat Profile screen, and both are rated safe. It is not in a conversation.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The app charges for priority routing, which Janitor+ sells (m02, l02), so this existing opportunity rewards a resource the app charges for.

c2_evidence.reason: The claims about Janitor+ selling priority routing (s02.e06) and the permanent Upgrade entry (s09.e31) are supported. The normal-priority free tier is inferred from s02.e07 (m03). The card, copy and cost remarks are the proposal's own additions or predictions.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The card is shown only to free users, and subscribers already have priority routing and never see it. The offer does not sit inside a paid-only screen.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 60 minutes and is capped at 2 per day, so it is a sample and not lasting access. Priority routing is already sold by the app, so the queue placement is not taken from anyone unsold.

c5_moment.reason: The card lives on the profile menu, a persistent surface the user chooses to open, and it interrupts no task in progress.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn rewarded playable, and the reward is granted only after the play is verified. The trigger, returning to the menu from Upgrade, is an app event.

c7_specific.reason: It names the Janitor+ priority routing benefit, the Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry and the profile menu drawer, so it would not read the same in another app.

other_concern: The Upgrade destination screen was not captured, so detecting a return from it without subscribing is an unverified assumption. The 'normal queue' wording also rests on inference only.
